title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.13212v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Actions specify what a robot should execute, but do not describe what those commands will achieve. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies nevertheless learn primarily by predicting action chunks from images, language, and state. We introduce Action--Future Coupled Effect Learning (AFCE), which makes a future-grounded physical Effect the policy's primary prediction target. An offline tokenizer constructs temporally ordered Effect tokens from demonstrated actions, realized robot responses, and sparse visual transitions. Reconstruction objectives encourage the representation to retain executable detail and observed physical change. A flow-matching VLA predicts Effects from current images, instruction, and robot state, while a state-conditioned decoder converts them into action chunks. translated_title: 超越动作：为视觉-语言-动作模型学习未来操作目标
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.13212v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：动作规定了机器人应该执行什么，但没有描述这些指令将会实现什么效果。然而，视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略目前主要通过从图像、语言和状态预测动作块来学习。我们提出了动作-未来耦合效果学习，该方法使基于未来的物理效果成为策略的主要预测目标。一个离线分词器从演示动作、机器人实际响应和稀疏视觉过渡中构建按时间排序的效果标记。重建目标鼓励该表示保留可执行的细节和观察到的物理变化。一个流匹配VLA从当前图像、指令和机器人状态预测效果，而状态条件解码器则将这些效果转换为动作块。特定于本体的接口使单臂和双臂任务能够共享同一个效果模型。在DexJoCo上，AFCE实现了50.97%的总体成功率，相比……有所提升。
tldr: 该论文提出动作-未来耦合效果学习，让视觉-语言-动作模型以未来物理效果而非动作本身作为主要预测目标，从而提升机器人策略的性能，在DexJoCo上达到50.97%的总体成功率。
